facts: True only for a REGRESSION against the baseline, the pageable signal.
Over the aspirational absolute budget. Reported, never paged: see the comment on `breach` in evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts.
Everything, regression first. Kept for callers that just want a blob.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: database-request-cost

ai.title: Database cost alert pages only on regressions, not over-budget
ai.summary: The database request cost evaluator now separates the over-budget signal from the regression signal so that a percentile can be flagged over budget and still compared to its baseline in the same pass. evaluateFamily returns { overBudget, regressed } instead of a single array, and the over-budget branch no longer short-circuits with continue. evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts sets verdict.breach to regressed.length > 0, meaning over-budget percentiles remain reported in the new verdict.overBudget array but never page the alert, while verdict.reasons stays regression-first via [...regressed, ...overBudget] for callers that want a flat blob.
ai.evidence: common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts: evaluateFamily now returns { overBudget, regressed } instead of a single array; the over-budget branch no longer continues so a percentile can populate overBudget and still be compared to its baseline in the same pass; evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts sets verdict.breach to regressed.length > 0; DatabaseCostVerdict gains explicit overBudget and regressed arrays with reasons built as [...regressed, ...overBudget].
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads the new overBudget and regressed fields or how the paging integration consumes verdict.breach.

ai.title: Add savings CTA analytics event
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_HOME_SAVINGS_CTA_CLICKED` to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. Fires alongside `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_CLICKED` with `savings`, `perSeat`, `seats`, `tools`, and `toolCount` properties. Enables bucketing click-through by computed savings value.

eli5.text: When you click the savings calculator on the homepage, a new tracking event is now recorded in addition to the existing download tracking, capturing the specific savings amount, per-seat pricing, seat count, selected tools, and total tool count at the moment of your click. This allows the analytics system to measure which computed savings values correlate with higher conversion rates by grouping visitors based on the savings figure they were shown before deciding to download. The change is live today and applies to all homepage visitors who interact with the savings calculator call-to-action.

eli5.text: A new coding assistant option called Buffy has been added that can now read only parts of files instead of whole files at once, and it can shrink down older conversation history so it stays focused during long coding sessions. When you work with Buffy, you will notice it asks you to search for what you need before reading files, and it will read specific sections of files rather than loading everything at once. The feature is turned on only when someone specifically chooses this new assistant, while the default way of working stays the same.

entries.title: Shared/Core update

ai.title: Foreign client signals detect non-freebuff traffic and downgrade
ai.summary: A new module adds `detectForeignFreebuffClient`, which inspects a request's `tools`, temperature, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, and `max_completion_tokens` fields to flag traffic that did not originate from a Freebuff client, and `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, which downgrades flagged requests to the `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` model according to one of four modes. The discriminator favors tool schemas over system prompts because a prompt is trivially copyable while tool names a harness dispatches on are not, and tool-based detection takes precedence over sampling-param detection so that real clients setting those params are never downgraded. Caller-controlled tool names are truncated to `MAX_LOGGED_TOOL_NAME_LENGTH` (64) and bounded to a sample of 8 before logging.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts` defines `FREEBUFF_DOWNGRADE_MODEL_ID` = 'inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free', `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES`, `detectForeignFreebuffClient`, `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, and the `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` / `ForeignClientVerdict` / `ForeignClientDecision` types.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` or which `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` the request path selects.

ai.title: base3 agent id suffix splits desktop thread metrics
ai.summary: Adds `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_THREAD_V3_SUFFIX` ('v3') and optional `agentGeneration` param to `getFreebuffDesktopThreadAgentId`. Base3 desktop threads now get distinct agent IDs (`freebuff-desktop-thread-{local|worktree}-v3`) to split spend/run counts by `agent_id` in DB during staggered base2/base3 rollout. Updates `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_THREAD_AGENT_IDS` and `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` to register the new base3 IDs against `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_MODELS`.

eli5.text: The desktop assistant now tracks two separate sets of usage numbers for free users: one for the older version (still called 'freebuff-desktop-thread') and one for the newer version, which gets a 'v3' tag appended to its name. This affects free desktop users who are gradually being moved to the new version, letting the product team compare how the old and new versions spend compute and run sessions side by side. If you looked at the internal billing database today, you would see usage records split into two clearly labeled buckets instead of being blended together, making the base2-to-base3 rollout measureable.

facts: Tool names we define that other agent harnesses also ship.

Maintained as an EXCLUSION list, with the signature derived from it, because the inclusion list rotted: `researcher-web` offers exactly `['web_search', 'read_url']`, and a hand-picked signature that happened to omit both flagged 100% of its 334,042 requests from 4,821 users over 30 days.

Any tool added to `toolNames` now joins the signature automatically, so the failure mode is a new *generic* name we forget to list here, which flags a third party we could already flag, rather than silently downgrading our own users.
Tool names that, on their own, mark a request as coming from one of our clients: everything we define that is not generic.

ai.title: Foreign client signal now derives signature tool set from tool names
ai.summary: The Freebuff signature-tool discriminator is rebuilt in `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts`: `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` is now derived from the shared `toolNames` list, minus the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion set, plus `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES` (set to `['decide']`). The `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type are removed from `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, so `foreign_toolset` is always enforced and `sampling_params` is always reported but never acted upon. This moves the signature from a brittle hand-maintained list to one that updates automatically whenever a new tool is added to `toolNames` or forgotten in `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES`, with the `decide` tool covering Freebuff Desktop's autorun agent.
ai.evidence: Modified `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts` (commit 68d9a88c): the hand-maintained `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` literal array is replaced with a derived set built from the imported `toolNames` in `common/src/tools/constants`, filtered to remove the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion list and combined with the new `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES = ['decide']`; the `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type on `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` are removed, so the function now always enforces `foreign_toolset` and always reports `sampling_params` without acting on it.
ai.migration: Requests to the Freebuff free endpoint that do not carry a distinctive Freebuff tool name will now always be served `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` instead of the originally requested model.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` updating to the new parameterless signature, or how the `mode` removal is reconciled downstream.

ai.title: Add deterministic verdict file to terminal broker smoke test
ai.summary: The `createConsoleReaderScript` function in `cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts` now accepts a `verdictPath` argument to write a completion marker after the CONIN$ probe resolves. This replaces a fixed `Bun.sleep(250)` wait with a `waitFor` check on the verdict file, preventing race conditions with PowerShell startup and ensuring stdout is flushed before the broker force-kills the process on Windows.

eli5.text: When the terminal broker smoke test runs a PowerShell script to check console availability, that script now writes a small 'done' file on disk only after it has actually finished its check and flushed its output, instead of the test just waiting a fixed quarter-second. The test now waits until that 'done' file appears before deciding whether the script leaked a console, which prevents it from aborting too early on slow or busy Windows machines where PowerShell hasn't finished starting up. If you watched the test's exchange directory, you'd see a new file named 'console-reader-verdict' appear after the script completes, and the test would reliably wait for it before proceeding.

ai.title: Root agent no tools signal joins the foreign client detection
ai.summary: A third signal, `root_agent_no_tools`, is added to `ForeignClientSignal` and to the detection flow in `detectForeignFreebuffClient`, which now takes an `isRootAgent` parameter threaded through `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`. When a root agent offers no tools, it reports the `root_agent_no_tools` signal, but because enforcement is deliberately avoided over real agentic traffic, only `foreign_toolset` still sets a `downgradeTo` value, which resolves to the `FREEBUFF_DOWNGRADE_MODEL_ID` constant already defined in the module.

The `downgradeTo` expression stays gated on `verdict.signal === 'foreign_toolset'`, so only that signal selects the `FREEBUFF_DOWNGRADE_MODEL_ID` constant.

facts: See researcher-web: without a trailing turn, a step that ends on a tool result lets the model stop after thinking and return no answer.

Without this, every step ends the conversation on a raw tool result and the model is never asked for anything, so it ends the step after thinking, no text, no tool call, and the spawner gets a thinking trace instead of the summary.
entries.title: Agents update: researcher-docs

ai.title: Add stepPrompt to researcher agents
ai.summary: Added `stepPrompt` to `researcher-docs.ts` and `researcher-web.ts`. This fixes a bug where steps ending on tool results caused the model to stop after thinking, returning no answer. The prompt explicitly instructs the model to continue with tool calls or a final answer.

eli5.text: Research agents now reliably finish their answers instead of going silent mid-task. You, as someone using these research tools, will notice that they produce a complete written summary at the end of each step rather than stopping right after fetching information, leaving you with nothing. The developers added an internal instruction that tells the agent to keep going, either make another search/fetch or write the final answer, so the step no longer ends on an empty thinking trace. This fix is already live in the two researcher agents that handle documentation and web research.

ai.title: Add utcDateKey helper to reddit-capi-events
ai.summary: Adds `utcDateKey` to `common/src/util/reddit-capi-events.ts` to standardize UTC day boundaries for D1/D7/D24 retention eligibility. This prevents lost conversions caused by memoization mismatches where local timezones (e.g., Pacific) lag behind UTC rollovers. The helper is isolated in a dependency-free module to avoid importing the database connection pool from `packages/internal/src/reddit-conversions.ts`.

eli5.text: If you run ads or track how people return to your app, your system used to guess 'did we already count today?' using your local clock, which can drift behind the global day. Now it decides that moment using a single, consistent UTC day boundary, so a late-hour Pacific user no longer slips through the cracks and loses their retention milestone. The new helper is a standalone utility that other code is instructed not to rebuild, and anything checking 'have we done this today?' is pointed at it. It is live today and only affects the day-boundary check; nothing else changes for you.
